Note.description: A page in the garden — a paper summary, a symptom log, a session note, an index. The only type that owns prose on the site.

Session.description: A dated event in the case: a self-administered test, a therapy conversation, a clinical appointment, a deliberate journalling pass. The unit of 'what we did and when'.

Symptom.description: An experienced pattern being tracked — described phenomenologically, not diagnostically.

Instrument.description: A measurement tool: a screener, a questionnaire, a cognitive task, a lab panel, a wearable metric.

Finding.description: A concrete result produced by a Session — a score, a clinician's observation, a lab value. Facts about the case, distinct from what they might mean.

Intervention.description: Something deliberately changed and tracked over time: medication, sleep protocol, therapy, exercise, caffeine, environment.

Mechanism.description: A named cognitive/neural construct the notebook reuses: response inhibition, statistical learning, mind-wandering, executive function.

Hypothesis.description: A load-bearing assertion the notebook is trying to defend or falsify. Never a diagnosis — always something that can be pressure-tested.

Question.description: An open problem the notebook is working on; can gate a Note, a Hypothesis, or a next Session.

Paper.description: An external work cited: journal article, preprint, book, clinical guideline.

Tension.description: A competing-explanation or trade-off held open on purpose — e.g. ADHD vs. anxiety as the source of the same symptom. Reified so it cannot quietly resolve itself.

Status.description: Lifecycle status (a hub-transit type: reachable but never traversed through).

partOf.description: Note belongs to a parent Note (section index).

covers.description: This note is where the thing is written up.

measures.description: Instrument is designed to measure this symptom domain or construct.

administeredIn.description: Instrument was administered during this session.

observedIn.description: Symptom was reported/observed in this session.

precedes.description: Session comes before another session — the timeline spine.

mayExplain.description: Candidate explanation for an experience or result. HYPOTHETICAL by construction — never a diagnosis.

affects.description: Intervention is being tracked for its effect on this.

derivesFrom.description: X is built on / specialises Y.

documentedIn.description: The case fact is written up in this note.

definedIn.description: Mechanism has its primary development in this note.

cites.description: Note cites a paper (a deliberate act, never inferred from prose).

dependsOn.description: Hypothesis rests on another hypothesis, on a question resolving a particular way, or on a finding holding up.

supports.description: Paper supports this hypothesis/mechanism. The edge carries the verbatim quote + page locator + confidence + rationale, so a fact and its justification travel together.

pressureTests.description: Paper challenges/qualifies this hypothesis/mechanism. Same evidence payload.

confounds.description: A rival explanation that must be ruled out before the hypothesis can stand. The honesty predicate of this ontology.

tensionWith.description: In unresolved tension with (both endpoints stay live).

supersedes.description: Replaces a prior version — later screening supersedes an earlier one, a revised hypothesis supersedes its draft.

flagsOpenQuestion.description: Flags an open question the node rests on.

wikiLinks.description: Wiki-style link parsed from prose. Navigation only — kept out of the argument graph.

structural.description: Where a thing sits: containment, coverage, what measures what.

temporal.description: The case timeline: what happened when, in what order, and what it produced.

causal.description: What might explain or affect what. Always hypothetical in this corpus.

provenance.description: Where a thing came from: which note records it, which paper, which author.

dialectical.description: What is contested: evidence, confounds, contradictions, supersession, open questions.

weak.description: Casual cross-links for navigation only — deliberately kept out of the argument graph.

nodes.label: 2026-07-26 — ASRS v1.1 self-screening & reflection
nodes.summary: Took the ASRS v1.1 (WHO-developed adult ADHD screener) and reflected on presentations and the 'calm outside, churning inside' pattern with a therapist who is themselves diagnosed with ADHD.

nodes.label: ASRS v1.1 (Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale)
nodes.summary: 18-item WHO-developed screener. Part A (6 items, cutoff ≥4) determines the screen; Part B (12 items) characterises symptom load. Deliberately tuned for sensitivity, so a positive screen is a reason to evaluate, not a diagnosis.

nodes.label: Cognitive Trade-off Task (ASRT + Go/No-Go)
nodes.summary: The paradigm used by Horváth et al. 2026: an Alternating Serial Reaction Time Task carrying a hidden probabilistic sequence (statistical learning) with an embedded Go/No-Go component (response inhibition), so both are measured at once rather than in isolation.

nodes.label: ASRS v1.1 Part A: 4/6 — positive screen
nodes.summary: Landed exactly at the cutoff on the six-item screener that determines the result. Part A is the most predictive component. Screening only — not a diagnosis.

nodes.label: ASRS v1.1 Part B: 6/12 supplementary symptoms
nodes.summary: Part B has no threshold; it describes which symptoms show up. Six indicates a meaningful additional symptom load, backing the Part A result.

nodes.label: No formal diagnosis as of 2026-07-26
nodes.summary: State of the record: a positive screen only. Everything downstream is hypothesis.

nodes.label: Disruptive internal state — calm outside, churning inside
nodes.summary: Outwardly calm and not fidgety, but a racing, unsettled mind — the DSM 'driven as if by a motor' item experienced mentally rather than behaviourally. The often-missed pattern in inattentive-leaning adults.

nodes.label: Inattentive pattern — sustaining focus, distractibility
nodes.summary: Consistent with a positive ASRS Part A and a lean toward the inattentive presentation.

nodes.label: Acting before thinking / impulsivity items
nodes.summary: Endorsed on the ASRS; the axis the Horváth paper probes directly via response inhibition.

nodes.label: Response inhibition
nodes.summary: The capacity to withhold a prepared response — indexed by No-Go accuracy. Consistently weaker at higher ADHD-trait load, even below clinical thresholds.

nodes.label: Statistical learning
nodes.summary: Implicit extraction of environmental regularities — the habit-learning system. Indexed by faster responses to high-probability triplets.

nodes.label: Inhibition–learning antagonism (competition hypothesis)
nodes.summary: The trade-off in which weaker inhibitory control normally buys stronger statistical learning. The paper's central object of study.

nodes.label: ADHD as a trait continuum
nodes.summary: The dimensional view: ADHD-like traits are distributed across the general population, and neurocognitive shifts appear before symptoms reach clinical significance. The frame that makes a screening score meaningful without a diagnosis.

nodes.label: Cue as motivational magnet (sign-tracking)
nodes.summary: Borrowed from animal sign-tracker/goal-tracker work: at high trait load the cue itself captures behaviour and top-down systems cannot override it — the authors' proposed reason the learning advantage breaks down.

nodes.label: Mind-wandering
nodes.summary: Spontaneous shift of attention from external demands to internally generated thought; offered as a second, transdiagnostic candidate mechanism.

nodes.label: Anxiety-driven arousal
nodes.summary: Chronic anxious arousal produces internal churn that is phenomenologically near-identical to internal hyperactivity, and frequently co-occurs with ADHD. The single most important thing to rule out here.

nodes.label: Sleep debt / disrupted sleep
nodes.summary: Insufficient or fragmented sleep degrades attention and produces restlessness — a mimic that must be excluded before attributing symptoms to ADHD.

nodes.label: Mood disturbance (depression / chronic stress)
nodes.summary: Depression and chronic stress produce concentration difficulty and inner agitation. Another mimic on the differential.

nodes.label: My disruptive internal state is ADHD-driven rather than anxiety-, sleep-, or mood-driven
nodes.summary: The load-bearing personal hypothesis. Three rival mechanisms confound it and none has been ruled out; it cannot advance until the internal state is described concretely.

nodes.label: My ASRS result places me on the ADHD trait continuum rather than in a yes/no category
nodes.summary: Framing rather than diagnosis: a Part A score at the cutoff situates me somewhere on a spectrum the literature treats dimensionally.

nodes.label: A positive ASRS screen warrants a full clinical evaluation
nodes.summary: The actionable claim. Holds regardless of how the ADHD-vs-mimics question resolves — the evaluation is what resolves it.

nodes.label: Higher ADHD-like traits are associated with weaker response inhibition
nodes.summary: Research-side claim, replicated by the Horváth study in a non-clinical sample and under dual-task load.

nodes.label: Rising ADHD-trait load progressively flattens the inhibition–learning trade-off
nodes.summary: The paper's core result: the compensatory learning advantage that normally accompanies weak inhibition breaks down at the high end of the trait continuum.

nodes.label: What does the 'disruptive internal state' actually consist of?
nodes.summary: Racing/jumping thoughts, a physical-but-invisible wound-up feeling, an inability to ever relax, or something else. These feel similar from the inside but point in different directions.
nodes.nextStep: Journal concrete examples as they happen, with time of day and context.

nodes.label: Is the internal restlessness driven by ADHD, anxiety, sleep, mood, or a combination?
nodes.summary: The differential. A good evaluator traces the symptom to its source rather than assuming the ADHD thread.
nodes.nextStep: Bring the differential explicitly to the evaluation; don't let it collapse into a single label.

nodes.label: Where would my ASRS score fall relative to the Horváth sample?
nodes.summary: The paper's sample scored M = 31.66, SD = 10.04 on the 18-item ASRS. My record currently stores Part A/Part B counts, not the summed dimensional score — so the comparison can't yet be made.
nodes.nextStep: Retain the item-level ASRS responses and compute the summed score.

nodes.label: What is the right next clinical step, and with whom?
nodes.summary: GP referral, psychologist, or psychiatrist — and what to bring to make the appointment productive.
nodes.nextStep: Draft a one-page summary for a clinician from the diagnostics note and the symptom log.

nodes.label: ADHD-like traits reshape the balance between inhibitory control and predictive processes
nodes.summary: n = 226 non-clinical sample; Cognitive Trade-off Task measuring response inhibition and statistical learning simultaneously; ADHD traits measured dimensionally with the ASRS v1.1.

nodes.label: The same internal restlessness fits ADHD and anxiety equally well
nodes.summary: Held open deliberately. Internal hyperactivity and anxious arousal are near-indistinguishable from the inside, they co-occur often, and depression/stress/sleep produce similar churn. Nothing in the record currently discriminates between them.

nodes.label: The evidence base doesn't obviously generalise to me
nodes.summary: The Horváth sample was 226 university students, 81% women, mean age 21.4, tested online without supervision. The authors themselves caution about generalisability to men and across the lifespan — so the dimensional framing is borrowed, not measured, for my case.

edges.quote: We found that higher ADHD-like traits were associated with poorer response inhibition, confirming previous research.
edges.rationale: Direct statement of the primary result in a non-clinical sample (n = 226), replicating a hallmark finding below diagnostic thresholds.

edges.quote: this learning advantage progressively diminished across the ADHD trait continuum, becoming markedly reduced in individuals with high symptom prevalence
edges.rationale: The paper's core claim; backed in Results by a significant three-way interaction (No-Go performance x ASRS x Triplet Type, F(1, 13046.16) = 4.36, p = .037).

edges.quote: a condition understood to exist along a continuum of traits in the general population
edges.rationale: States the dimensional framing the whole design rests on — the reason a screening score is meaningful without a diagnosis.

edges.quote: we uncovered an antagonistic relationship between inhibition and statistical learning: weaker inhibitory control was linked to enhanced learning of environmental regularities
edges.rationale: Simple-effects analysis: learning effect b = -9.40 at low No-Go accuracy vs. b = -2.92 at high accuracy, all pairwise contrasts significant.

edges.quote: the No-Go signal may function as a motivational magnet that triggers an automatic response
edges.rationale: Explicitly framed by the authors as a hypothesised interpretation borrowed from animal sign-tracker research, not a measured mechanism.

edges.quote: Another angle of interpretation emerges from research on mind wandering, the spontaneous shift of attention from external demands to internally generated thought
edges.rationale: Offered as a secondary, transdiagnostic candidate; not measured in this study. Relevant here only because it is the closest published construct to the 'churning inside' description.

edges.quote: our sample consisted primarily of university students, which resulted in a narrow age range and high educational attainment. While this population is common in cognitive research, it may not be fully representative of the general population.
edges.rationale: The authors' own generalisability caveat — borrowing their continuum to place a non-student adult is an extrapolation.

edges.quote: there was a significant gender imbalance in our sample, with 81% identifying as women ... our results should be interpreted with caution regarding their generalizability to men
edges.rationale: Response-inhibition findings are the least sex-robust part of the result, and inhibition is exactly the axis the reshaping claim runs through.

edges.quote: Another limitation concerns the exclusive reliance on the ASRS (Kessler et al., 2005; v1.1) for estimating ADHD-like traits. While self-report questionnaires are efficient and widely validated for dimensional studies in the general population, they may lack the precision of multi-instrument or multi-informant approaches.
edges.rationale: The continuum is only as good as the instrument locating people on it — the same instrument this notebook's single data point comes from.
